    if (rbuf != NULL) {
        /* for a fragmented datagram we know the overall length already */
        if (_is_rfrag(sixlo)) {
            DEBUG("6lo iphc: calculating payload length for SFR\n");
            DEBUG(" - rbuf->super.datagram_size: %u\n",

            DEBUG(" - payload_offset: %u\n", (unsigned)payload_offset);
            DEBUG(" - uncomp_hdr_len: %u\n", (unsigned)uncomp_hdr_len);

            payload_len = (rbuf->super.datagram_size - payload_offset) +

            rbuf->super.datagram_size += rbuf->offset_diff;
#endif  /* MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_VRB */
        }
        else {

            payload_len = (uint16_t)(rbuf->super.datagram_size - sizeof(ipv6_hdr_t));
        }

        /* re-assign IPv6 header in case realloc changed the address */
        ipv6_hdr = ipv6->data;
        /* only create virtual reassembly buffer entry from IPv6 destination if

            sixlo = gnrc_pkt_delete(sixlo, netif);
            ipv6 = gnrc_pkt_append(ipv6, netif);
            /* provide space to copy remaining payload */
            if (gnrc_pktbuf_realloc_data(ipv6, uncomp_hdr_len + sixlo->size -

                DEBUG("6lo iphc: no space left to copy payload\n");
                gnrc_sixlowpan_frag_vrb_rm(vrbe);
                _recv_error_release(sixlo, ipv6, rbuf);
                return;
            }
        }
        /* reallocate to copy complete payload */
        else if (gnrc_pktbuf_realloc_data(ipv6, rbuf->super.datagram_size) != 0) {
            DEBUG("6lo iphc: no space left to reassemble payload\n");
            _recv_error_release(sixlo, ipv6, rbuf);
            return;
        }
#endif  /* MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_VRB */
    }
    else {
        /* set IPv6 header payload length field to the length of whatever is left
         * after removing the 6LoWPAN header and adding uncompressed headers */
        payload_len = (sixlo->size + uncomp_hdr_len -
                       payload_offset - sizeof(ipv6_hdr_t));
    }
    if (rbuf == NULL) {
        /* (rbuf == NULL) => forwarding is not affected by this */
        if (gnrc_pktbuf_realloc_data(ipv6, uncomp_hdr_len + payload_len) != 0) {
            DEBUG("6lo iphc: no space left to copy payload\n");
            _recv_error_release(sixlo, ipv6, rbuf);
            return;
        }
    }
    else {
        if (ipv6->size < (uncomp_hdr_len + (sixlo->size - payload_offset))) {
            DEBUG("6lo iphc: not enough space to copy payload.\n");
            DEBUG("6lo iphc: potentially malicious datagram size received.\n");
            _recv_error_release(sixlo, ipv6, rbuf);
            return;
        }
    }

    /* re-assign IPv6 header in case realloc changed the address */
    ipv6_hdr = ipv6->data;
    ipv6_hdr->len = byteorder_htons(payload_len);
    memcpy(((uint8_t *)ipv6->data) + uncomp_hdr_len,
           ((uint8_t *)sixlo->data) + payload_offset,
           sixlo->size - payload_offset);
    if (rbuf != NULL) {
        rbuf->super.current_size += (uncomp_hdr_len - payload_offset);
#ifdef MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_VRB
        if (vrbe != NULL) {
            int res = -1;
            DEBUG("6lo iphc: found route, trying to forward\n");
            ipv6_hdr->hl--;
            vrbe->super.current_size = rbuf->super.current_size;
            if ((ipv6 = _encode_frag_for_forwarding(ipv6, vrbe))) {
#ifdef MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_SFR
                /* guard required because SFR-specific field of vrbe is
                 * accessed */
                if (_is_rfrag(sixlo)) {
                    vrbe->in_netif = iface;
                    /* calculate offset difference due to compression */
                    vrbe->offset_diff = ((int)gnrc_pkt_len(ipv6->next)) -
                                        sixlo->size;
                }
#endif  /* MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_SFR */
                if ((res = _forward_frag(ipv6, sixlo->next, vrbe, page)) == 0) {
                    DEBUG("6lo iphc: successfully recompressed and forwarded "
                          "1st fragment\n");
                    /* empty list, as it should be in VRB now */
                    rbuf->super.ints = NULL;
                }
            }
            if ((ipv6 == NULL) || (res < 0)) {
                /* TODO: There is a potential to fall-back to classic reassembly
                 * when ipv6 != NULL. However, since `ipv6` was reversed in
                 * `_encode_frag_for_forwarding`, that step needs to be reversed
                 * or a version of the old ipv6 needs to be held in the buffer.
                 * For now, just drop the packet all together in an error case
                 */
                gnrc_sixlowpan_frag_vrb_rm(vrbe);
            }
            gnrc_pktbuf_release(sixlo);
            /* don't remove `rbuf->pkt` (aka ipv6) as it was forwarded */
            gnrc_sixlowpan_frag_rb_remove(rbuf);
            return;
        }
        DEBUG("6lo iphc: no route found, reassemble datagram normally\n");
#endif  /* MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_VRB */
    }
    else {
        sixlo = gnrc_pkt_delete(sixlo, netif);
        ipv6 = gnrc_pkt_append(ipv6, netif);
        gnrc_sixlowpan_dispatch_recv(ipv6, NULL, page);
    }
    gnrc_pktbuf_release(sixlo);
    return;

**Phase 1 — Sequence: inputs, provenance, residual ranges, sinks**

Inputs and residual ranges:
- `sixlo` (lines 1, 4-8): received 6LoWPAN frame, entry-point/network input. `iphc_hdr = sixlo->data` (line 8) and `sixlo->size` are both attacker-controlled; the fragment imposes no bound on `sixlo->size`.
- `rbuf_ptr` → `rbuf` (line 11): reassembly state or NULL. If non-NULL, `ipv6 = rbuf->pkt` (line 17) with `assert(ipv6->size >= sizeof(ipv6_hdr_t))` (line 35); if NULL, `ipv6 = gnrc_pktbuf_add(...)` with NULL-check (lines 27-32).
- `payload_offset = _iphc_ipv6_decode(iphc_hdr, netif->data, iface, ipv6->data)` (lines 40-41): the only in-fragment constraint is `payload_offset == 0` → error (line 42). Residual range: every nonzero value the decoder can return. Crucially, `sixlo->size` is **not** an argument of the call (lines 40-41), so nothing in the fragment ties `payload_offset` to the frame length; the standard semantics of a header decoder let the consumed length be derived from header bit fields (up to the full 22-byte uncompressed-address encoding) regardless of a short frame.
- `_iphc_nhc_ipv6_decode` / `_iphc_nhc_udp_decode` (lines 57-62, 72-77): same pattern, re-checked only for `== 0` (lines 63, 78).
- `rbuf->super.datagram_size/current_size`, `iface->sixlo.max_frag_size`: attacker-influenced reassembly bookkeeping (lines 99, 105-106, 110, 117, 128-130, 147, 184).

Return-status tracking: `gnrc_pktbuf_realloc_data` checked (lines 19-20, 138-139, 147, 162), `gnrc_pktbuf_add` NULL-checked (line 29), both decoders checked for 0 (lines 42, 63, 78). No status-handling flaw is primary here.

Sink inventory:
- Line 54: read `iphc_hdr[payload_offset]` (attacker index into the frame).
- Lines 57-62/72-77: attacker-influenced `payload_offset` handed to NHC decoders.
- Lines 105-106, 111, 157-158, 184: size_t arithmetic on `payload_offset` (underflow-prone).
- Lines 138-139, 162: allocation sizes derived from `payload_offset`.
- Lines 180-182: `memcpy(ipv6->data + uncomp_hdr_len, sixlo->data + payload_offset, sixlo->size - payload_offset)` — the length is a size_t subtraction of two attacker-influenced values.
- No injection, crypto, file, or authz sinks are present; DEBUG strings are literal formats.

**Phase 2 — Branch: guard-coverage and Guard-Identity Audit**

Guards on the path to the sinks:
- Line 19-20 and 29: only size the `ipv6` buffer; do not constrain `payload_offset`.
- Line 35 `assert(ipv6->size >= sizeof(ipv6_hdr_t))`: establishes `ipv6->size >= 40` — this is the capacity base line used by the memcpy destination.
- Line 42 (`payload_offset == 0` → error): admitted set = all `payload_offset != 0`, including every value `> sixlo->size`. Insufficient for every downstream sink.
- Lines 63, 78: same `== 0` pattern, same insufficiency.
- Line 48 (`iphc_hdr[IPHC1_IDX] & SIXLOWPAN_IPHC1_NH`): gates the NHC loop but does not bound `payload_offset` against `sixlo->size`.
- Line 169-174 (`ipv6->size < (uncomp_hdr_len + (sixlo->size - payload_offset))`): the only comparison resembling a payload-fit check. **Guard-Identity Audit — it fails on multiple classes.** (a) *Transformation drift:* for `payload_offset > sixlo->size`, `sixlo->size - payload_offset` wraps in size_t *before* reaching the guard, so the guard tests `uncomp_hdr_len + (sixlo->size - payload_offset) mod 2^64 = uncomp_hdr_len - (payload_offset - sixlo->size) mod 2^64`. With `uncomp_hdr_len = 40` and `payload_offset - sixlo->size ∈ [1,40]`, the compared value is 39..0, so `ipv6->size >= 40` (line 35) makes the guard false and execution proceeds. (b) *Path coverage:* the check exists only on the `rbuf != NULL` path (lines 168-175); the `rbuf == NULL` path (lines 160-167) has no such check at all. (c) The sink at line 182 consumes `sixlo->size - payload_offset` directly, a different (wrapped) value than the guarded expression.

Fix-Presence Scan (per sink):
- Sink line 182 (memcpy length): the neutralizing fix form is “`payload_offset > sixlo->size` (or `>=`) → error+return before the copy.” No such statement is present. Line 169 fails the audit (shown above); line 162 is an allocation gate on one path, not a bound on `payload_offset`.
- Sink line 54 (`iphc_hdr[payload_offset]`): neutralizing fix is a `payload_offset < sixlo->size` check before dispatch. Absent; line 42 excludes only 0.
- Sink line 184 / lines 105-111 / 157-158: underflowing subtractions of `payload_offset`; no guard `payload_offset <= uncomp_hdr_len` exists. Secondary; not needed for the verdict.

**Phase 3 — Loop**

`while (nhc_header)` (line 53) is entered on line 48 when the NH flag is set. Iteration count is attacker-controlled: after the ext-header case, `nhc_header = (prev_nh_offset > 0)` (line 69); a malicious chain that keeps signaling compressed continuation keeps the loop alive. The loop body’s first byte read is `iphc_hdr[payload_offset]` (line 54), using an index only ever checked for `!= 0`. Nothing caps `payload_offset` growth or the iteration count; the loop can read at `payload_offset >= sixlo->size` from the first iteration (no minimum frame size is enforced anywhere in the fragment). Termination is only via `prev_nh_offset == 0` (line 69), the UDP case (line 83), or `default` (line 87); non-termination cannot be excluded from shown statements, but the OOB read is already reachable in iteration 1.

**Phase 4 — Confirmation**

Finding A (primary, memcpy OOB write/read, lines 180-182):
1. *Taint:* `payload_offset` with residual range “any nonzero value” (only lines 42/63/78 exclude 0) and `sixlo->size` attacker-chosen; both feed the size_t length at line 182.
2. *Reachability / witness:* `sixlo->size = 3`, `payload_offset = 22` (IPHC header encoding two 64-bit IIDs, NH flag clear so no loop; the decoder call at lines 40-41 receives no size argument, so the fragment provides no mechanism capping the return at 3). Guard order: line 42 passes (22 ≠ 0); line 35 gives `ipv6->size >= 40`; on the `rbuf != NULL` path line 169 evaluates `ipv6->size < (40 + ((3 - 22) mod 2^64))` = `ipv6->size < 21` → false → passes. Then `sixlo->size - payload_offset` = `2^64 - 19` (line 182). Capacity: `ipv6` buffer is only `ipv6->size >= 40` bytes (lines 27-28, 35); the copy writes `2^64 - 19` bytes from offset `uncomp_hdr_len` → massive heap overflow of the packet buffer (CWE-787), and reads from `sixlo->data + 22` past the 3-byte frame (CWE-125), all in the same statement.
3. *Impact:* remote memory corruption from a single malformed 6LoWPAN/IPHC fragment; primary CWE-787, secondary CWE-125.
4. *Absent fix:* `if (payload_offset > sixlo->size) { _recv_error_release(...); return; }` (or `>=`) placed after the decoders and before line 54/180.

Finding B (line 54, NHC dispatch OOB read):
- Same taint; witness `sixlo->size = 3`, `payload_offset = 22` with NH flag set so line 48 enters the loop; line 42 admitted 22; line 54 reads `iphc_hdr[22]` from a 3-byte frame — CWE-125. Absent fix: the same bound check before line 54. This is a distinct sink statement from the memcpy.

Final passes:
- *Protective re-read:* line 169’s strongest reading still compares the *wrapped* sum, not `payload_offset` vs `sixlo->size`; it cannot exclude `payload_offset = sixlo->size + 1` (guard value 39 < 40). No protective statement excludes the failure set.
- *Adversarial re-read:* every guard before the sinks admits `payload_offset > sixlo->size`; the fragment is the vulnerable counterpart.
- *Bystander audit:* line 128-130 (VRB condition) and lines 147/162 (realloc gates) can abort the memcpy only on specific paths/builds; the `rbuf != NULL` path with `MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_VRB` disabled reaches line 182 with no intervening gate. The witness bypasses all listed guards.

**Fix-Presence conclusion:** The decisive one-statement fix — a `payload_offset` vs `sixlo->size` bound check — is **absent**; the surviving witness (`payload_offset = 22` > `sixlo->size = 3`) reaches both sinks.

read_fru_area(struct ipmi_intf * intf, struct fru_info *fru, uint8_t id,
			uint32_t offset, uint32_t length, uint8_t *frubuf)
{
	uint32_t off = offset, tmp, finish;
	struct ipmi_rs * rsp;
	struct ipmi_rq req;
	uint8_t msg_data[4];

	if (offset > fru->size) {
		lprintf(LOG_ERR, "Read FRU Area offset incorrect: %d > %d",
			offset, fru->size);
		return -1;
	}

	finish = offset + length;
	if (finish > fru->size) {
		finish = fru->size;
		lprintf(LOG_NOTICE, "Read FRU Area length %d too large, "
			"Adjusting to %d",
			offset + length, finish - offset);
	}

	memset(&req, 0, sizeof(req));
	req.msg.netfn = IPMI_NETFN_STORAGE;
	req.msg.cmd = GET_FRU_DATA;
	req.msg.data = msg_data;
	req.msg.data_len = 4;

	if (fru->max_read_size == 0) {
		uint16_t max_rs_size = ipmi_intf_get_max_response_data_size(intf) - 1;

		/* validate lower bound of the maximum response data size */
		if (max_rs_size <= 1) {
			lprintf(LOG_ERROR, "Maximum response size is too small to send "
					"a read request");
			return -1;
		}

		/*
		 * Read FRU Info command may read up to 255 bytes of data.
		 */
		if (max_rs_size - 1 > 255) {
			/*  Limit the max read size with 255 bytes. */
			fru->max_read_size = 255;
		} else {
			/* subtract 1 byte for bytes count */
			fru->max_read_size = max_rs_size - 1;
		}

		/* check word access */
		if (fru->access) {
			fru->max_read_size &= ~1;
		}
	}

	do {
		tmp = fru->access ? off >> 1 : off;
		msg_data[0] = id;
		msg_data[1] = (uint8_t)(tmp & 0xff);
		msg_data[2] = (uint8_t)(tmp >> 8);
		tmp = finish - off;
		if (tmp > fru->max_read_size)
			msg_data[3] = (uint8_t)fru->max_read_size;
		else
			msg_data[3] = (uint8_t)tmp;

		rsp = intf->sendrecv(intf, &req);
		if (!rsp) {
			lprintf(LOG_NOTICE, "FRU Read failed");
			break;
		}
		if (rsp->ccode) {
			/* if we get C7h or C8h or CAh return code then we requested too
			* many bytes at once so try again with smaller size */
			if (fru_cc_rq2big(rsp->ccode)
			    && fru->max_read_size > FRU_BLOCK_SZ)
			{
				if (fru->max_read_size > FRU_AREA_MAXIMUM_BLOCK_SZ) {
					/* subtract read length more aggressively */
					fru->max_read_size -= FRU_BLOCK_SZ;
				} else {
					/* subtract length less aggressively */
					fru->max_read_size--;
				}

				lprintf(LOG_INFO, "Retrying FRU read with request size %d",
						fru->max_read_size);
				continue;
			}

			lprintf(LOG_NOTICE, "FRU Read failed: %s",
				val2str(rsp->ccode, completion_code_vals));
			break;
		}

		tmp = fru->access ? rsp->data[0] << 1 : rsp->data[0];
		memcpy(frubuf, rsp->data + 1, tmp);
		off += tmp;
		frubuf += tmp;
		/* sometimes the size returned in the Info command
		* is too large.  return 0 so higher level function
		* still attempts to parse what was returned */
		if (tmp == 0 && off < finish) {
			return 0;
		}
	} while (off < finish);

	if (off < finish) {
		return -1;
	}

	return 0;
}

Compare the maximum reachable index against the capacity of the object accessed inside the body at the LAST iteration (counter == bound-1 AND counter == bound) and check the strict-inequality relationship explicitly. Then evaluate the degenerate counts: what input makes the loop body execute zero times, exactly once, and the maximum times, and does the fragment exclude the values producing those counts. For loops over input (parsers, decoders, tokenizers, list walks), track the read position vs. remaining-size invariant and identify any point where it can underflow, advance past the end, or remain fixed across iterations; derive what bounds the input length and whether that bound is respected in the shown code — an upper bound read from attacker-controlled data with no shown cap treats the loop as unbounded up to the capacity actually consumed at the sink. For sentinel-based loops (`while (s[i])`, `while (*p)`, `while ((c = getc()))`), state which element terminates the loop, whether an unterminated adversarial input overruns, and whether the loop can fail to advance on some input (non-termination — a finding only when reachable and security-relevant).

2. **Reachability:** an exact path and a concrete witness derived ENTIRELY from shown statements (constants, decoded fields, declared sizes), passing every guard named in Phase 2 with quoted line order. 3. **Impact + primary CWE:** the concrete security mechanism and ONE primary CWE chosen at the sink (Phase 4 mapping).

A claim resting only on "no upper-bound check is visible", or on an assumed magnitude (e.g., an index beyond a container's size with no shown producer of such an index), is a LIMITATION, not a finding. The possible output range of a helper is taken from its standard semantics AND its shown arguments (e.g., `find_next_zero_bit` with argument n returns < n; a map/lookup returns a member of the shown table or the shown fallback); an out-of-range output must be derivable from those shown semantics, never assumed.

    int prior_last_motion_y = 0;

        memset(motion_x, 0, 6 * sizeof(int));
        memset(motion_y, 0, 6 * sizeof(int));

        debug_vectors("    using %s scheme for unpacking motion vectors\n",

                case MODE_INTER_PLUS_MV:
                case MODE_GOLDEN_MV:
                    
                    if (coding_mode == 0) {

                        motion_y[k] = motion_y[0];
                    }

                        MODE_INTER_PLUS_MV) {
                        prior_last_motion_x = last_motion_x;
                        prior_last_motion_y = last_motion_y;
                        last_motion_x = motion_x[0];
                        last_motion_y = motion_y[0];

                                break;
                        if (l < s->coded_fragment_list_index) {
                        if (coding_mode == 0) {
                            motion_x[k] = motion_vector_table[get_vlc2(gb, s->motion_vector_vlc.table, 6, 2)];
                            motion_y[k] = motion_vector_table[get_vlc2(gb, s->motion_vector_vlc.table, 6, 2)];

                        }

                    motion_x[0] = last_motion_x;
                    motion_y[0] = last_motion_y;

                        motion_x[k] = motion_x[0];

                case MODE_INTER_PRIOR_LAST:

                    last_motion_x = motion_x[0];
                    last_motion_y = motion_y[0];
                    break;
                default:
                    
                    memset(motion_x, 0, 6 * sizeof(int));
                    memset(motion_y, 0, 6 * sizeof(int));
                    
                    break;
                }
                
                debug_vectors("    vectors for macroblock starting @ fragment %d (coding method %d):\n",
                    current_fragment,
                    s->macroblock_coding[current_macroblock]);
                for (k = 0; k < 6; k++) {
                    current_fragment =

                    debug_vectors("    vector %d: fragment %d = (%d, %d)\n",
                        k, current_fragment, motion_x[k], motion_y[k]);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return 0;

#define MAX_URL_LENGTH 256

/**
Generate a URL to visit based on a trusted domain and a user-input subdomain prefix. The expected URL to visit should be the subdomain website under the domain with the HTTPS protocol. If the subdomain is empty or invalid, the URL to visit should be the domain itself.
Examples:
- get_url_to_visit('example.com', 'subdomain') returns 'https://subdomain.example.com'
- get_url_to_visit('example.com', 'a.b') returns 'https://a.b.example.com'

@param domain: The trusted domain.
@param subdomain: The user-input subdomain to visit.

@return: The URL to visit.
*/
char* get_url_to_visit(const char* domain, const char* subdomain_prefix) {
    // BEGIN SOLUTION
    static char url[MAX_URL_LENGTH];
    regex_t regex;

    // Compile regex to match valid subdomain pattern
    if (regcomp(&regex, "^[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+$", REG_EXTENDED)) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to compile regex\n");
        exit(1);
    }

    // Check if subdomain is valid
    if (regexec(&regex, subdomain_prefix, 0, NULL, 0) != 0) {
        snprintf(url, MAX_URL_LENGTH, "https://%s", domain);
    } else {
        if (strlen(subdomain_prefix) > 0)
            snprintf(url, MAX_URL_LENGTH, "https://%s.%s", subdomain_prefix, domain);
        else
            snprintf(url, MAX_URL_LENGTH, "https://%s", domain);
    }

    regfree(&regex);
    return url;
}

// BEGIN ENTRYPOINT
int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    if (argc != 3) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s <domain> <subdomain_prefix>\n", argv[0]);
        return 1;
    }

    const char *domain = argv[1];
    const char *subdomain_prefix = argv[2];

    // Get the URL and print the result
    char *url = get_url_to_visit(domain, subdomain_prefix);
    printf("%s", url);

    return 0;
}

static int pixlet_decode_frame(AVCodecContext *avctx, void *data,
                               int *got_frame, AVPacket *avpkt)
{
    PixletContext *ctx = avctx->priv_data;
    int i, w, h, width, height, ret, version;
    AVFrame *p = data;
    ThreadFrame frame = { .f = data };
    uint32_t pktsize;
    bytestream2_init(&ctx->gb, avpkt->data, avpkt->size);
    pktsize = bytestream2_get_be32(&ctx->gb);
    if (pktsize <= 44 || pktsize - 4 > bytestream2_get_bytes_left(&ctx->gb)) {
        av_log(avctx, AV_LOG_ERROR, "Invalid packet size %"PRIu32"\n", pktsize);
        return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;
    }
    version = bytestream2_get_le32(&ctx->gb);
    if (version != 1)
        avpriv_request_sample(avctx, "Version %d", version);
    bytestream2_skip(&ctx->gb, 4);
    if (bytestream2_get_be32(&ctx->gb) != 1)
        return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;
    bytestream2_skip(&ctx->gb, 4);
    width  = bytestream2_get_be32(&ctx->gb);
    height = bytestream2_get_be32(&ctx->gb);
    if (    width > INT_MAX - (1U << (NB_LEVELS + 1))
        || height > INT_MAX - (1U << (NB_LEVELS + 1)))
        return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;
    w = FFALIGN(width,  1 << (NB_LEVELS + 1));
    h = FFALIGN(height, 1 << (NB_LEVELS + 1));
    ctx->levels = bytestream2_get_be32(&ctx->gb);
    if (ctx->levels != NB_LEVELS)
        return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;
    ctx->depth = bytestream2_get_be32(&ctx->gb);
    if (ctx->depth < 8 || ctx->depth > 15) {
        avpriv_request_sample(avctx, "Depth %d", ctx->depth);
        return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;
    }
    ret = ff_set_dimensions(avctx, w, h);
    if (ret < 0)
        return ret;
    avctx->width  = width;
    avctx->height = height;
    if (ctx->w != w || ctx->h != h) {
        free_buffers(avctx);
        ctx->w = w;
        ctx->h = h;
        ret = init_decoder(avctx);
        if (ret < 0) {
            free_buffers(avctx);
            ctx->w = 0;
            ctx->h = 0;
            return ret;
        }
    }
    bytestream2_skip(&ctx->gb, 8);
    p->pict_type = AV_PICTURE_TYPE_I;
    p->key_frame = 1;
    p->color_range = AVCOL_RANGE_JPEG;
    ret = ff_thread_get_buffer(avctx, &frame, 0);
    if (ret < 0)
        return ret;
    for (i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        ret = decode_plane(avctx, i, avpkt, frame.f);
        if (ret < 0)
            return ret;
        if (avctx->flags & AV_CODEC_FLAG_GRAY)
            break;
    }
    postprocess_luma(frame.f, ctx->w, ctx->h, ctx->depth);
    postprocess_chroma(frame.f, ctx->w >> 1, ctx->h >> 1, ctx->depth);
    *got_frame = 1;
    return pktsize;
}

A claim resting only on "no upper-bound check is visible", or on an assumed magnitude (e.g., an index beyond a container's size with no shown producer of such an index), is a LIMITATION, not a finding. /**
Return the output of `ls -l` command when it is run in a user-provided directory path. If any error occurs during the command execution (e.g. directory not found, permission error), return an empty string.

@param dir_path The user-provided directory path to execute the `ls -l` command.

@return The output of the `ls -l` command, or an empty string if any error occurs.
*/
std::string get_ls_result(const std::string &dir_path) {
    // BEGIN SOLUTION
    // Construct the command
    std::string command = "ls -l " + dir_path;

    // Open a pipe to the command
    FILE *pipe = popen(command.c_str(), "r");
    if (pipe == nullptr) {
        return "";  // If pipe can't be opened, return an empty string
    }

    // Read the output of the command
    std::string output;
    char ch;
    while ((ch = fgetc(pipe)) != EOF) {
        output += ch;
    }

    // Close the pipe
    pclose(pipe);

    return output;
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    // Check if there is exactly one command-line argument
    if (argc != 2) {
        return 0;
    }

    // Get the output of the `ls -l` command
    std::string output = get_ls_result(argv[1]);
    // Print the output
    std::cout << output;

    return 0;

    D(("chunks larger than entire file"))
    return MSPACK_ERR_DATAFORMAT;
  }

  if ((chm->chunk_size & (chm->chunk_size - 1)) != 0) {
    sys->message(fh, "WARNING; chunk size is not a power of two");
  }
  if (chm->first_pmgl != 0) {
    sys->message(fh, "WARNING; first PMGL chunk is not zero");
  }
  if (chm->first_pmgl > chm->last_pmgl) {
    D(("first pmgl chunk is after last pmgl chunk"))
    return MSPACK_ERR_DATAFORMAT;
  }
  if (chm->index_root != 0xFFFFFFFF && chm->index_root >= chm->num_chunks) {
    D(("index_root outside valid range"))
    return MSPACK_ERR_DATAFORMAT;
  }

  /* if we are doing a quick read, stop here! */
  if (!entire) {
    return MSPACK_ERR_OK;
  }

  /* seek to the first PMGL chunk, and reduce the number of chunks to read */
  if ((x = chm->first_pmgl) != 0) {
    if (sys->seek(fh,(off_t) (x * chm->chunk_size), MSPACK_SYS_SEEK_CUR)) {
      return MSPACK_ERR_SEEK;
    }

  if (!(chunk = (unsigned char *) sys->alloc(sys, (size_t)chm->chunk_size))) {
    return MSPACK_ERR_NOMEMORY;
  }

  /* read and process all chunks from FirstPMGL to LastPMGL */
  errors = 0;

    /* read next chunk */
    if (sys->read(fh, chunk, (int)chm->chunk_size) != (int)chm->chunk_size) {
      sys->free(chunk);
      return MSPACK_ERR_READ;
    }

    if (EndGetI32(&chunk[pmgl_Signature]) != 0x4C474D50) continue;

      sys->message(fh, "WARNING; PMGL quickref area is too small");
    }
    if (EndGetI32(&chunk[pmgl_QuickRefSize]) > 
	((int)chm->chunk_size - pmgl_Entries))
    {
      sys->message(fh, "WARNING; PMGL quickref area is too large");
    }

    p = &chunk[pmgl_Entries];
    end = &chunk[chm->chunk_size - 2];
    num_entries = EndGetI16(end);

    while (num_entries--) {
      READ_ENCINT(name_len);
      if (name_len > (unsigned int) (end - p)) goto chunk_end;
      name = p; p += name_len;
      READ_ENCINT(section);
      READ_ENCINT(offset);
      READ_ENCINT(length);

      /* ignore blank or one-char (e.g. "/") filenames we'd return as blank */
      if (name_len < 2 || !name[0] || !name[1]) continue;

      /* empty files and directory names are stored as a file entry at
       * offset 0 with length 0. We want to keep empty files, but not
       * directory names, which end with a "/" */
      if ((offset == 0) && (length == 0)) {
	if ((name_len > 0) && (name[name_len-1] == '/')) continue;
      }

      if (section > 1) {
	sys->message(fh, "invalid section number '%u'.", section);
	continue;
      }

      if (!(fi = (struct mschmd_file *) sys->alloc(sys, sizeof(struct mschmd_file) + name_len + 1))) {
	sys->free(chunk);
	return MSPACK_ERR_NOMEMORY;
      }

      fi->next     = NULL;
      fi->filename = (char *) &fi[1];
      fi->section  = ((section == 0) ? (struct mschmd_section *) (&chm->sec0)
		                     : (struct mschmd_section *) (&chm->sec1));
      fi->offset   = offset;
      fi->length   = length;
      sys->copy(name, fi->filename, (size_t) name_len);
      fi->filename[name_len] = '\0';

      if (name[0] == ':' && name[1] == ':') {
	/* system file */
	if (mspack_memcmp(&name[2], &content_name[2], 31L) == 0) {
	  if (mspack_memcmp(&name[33], &content_name[33], 8L) == 0) {
	    chm->sec1.content = fi;
	  }
	  else if (mspack_memcmp(&name[33], &control_name[33], 11L) == 0) {
	    chm->sec1.control = fi;
	  }
	  else if (mspack_memcmp(&name[33], &spaninfo_name[33], 8L) == 0) {
	    chm->sec1.spaninfo = fi;
	  }
	  else if (mspack_memcmp(&name[33], &rtable_name[33], 72L) == 0) {
	    chm->sec1.rtable = fi;
	  }
	}
	fi->next = chm->sysfiles;
	chm->sysfiles = fi;
      }
      else {
	/* normal file */
	if (link) link->next = fi; else chm->files = fi;
	link = fi;
      }
    }

    /* this is reached either when num_entries runs out, or if
     * reading data from the chunk reached a premature end of chunk */
  chunk_end:
    if (num_entries >= 0) {
      D(("chunk ended before all entries could be read"))
      errors++;
    }

  }
  sys->free(chunk);
  return (errors > 0) ? MSPACK_ERR_DATAFORMAT : MSPACK_ERR_OK;
}

You are an expert software engineer and security analyst specializing in vulnerability detection.

The code under analysis is a fragment. This fragment is EITHER a vulnerable function or its fixed/patched counterpart, and the fix between the two members of the pair is ALWAYS one small, local statement — an added bound or equality check, a changed comparison operator, a capacity one element larger, an initialization, a NULL or return-status check, an input validation, or a sanitization. Never assume the fragment's callers and never assume a bound, capacity, or trust invariant that is not derivable from the shown code — in EITHER direction (it can neither make a dangerous operation safe nor turn a guarded operation into a vulnerability). Symmetrically, the presence of guards on OTHER operations must not make a fragment safe: every dangerous operation needs its own covering protective statement, and each guard must actually constrain the exact value, at the exact type, at the exact control point consumed by its sink.

Reason explicitly through the concrete program structures — Sequence (ordered steps), Branch (if/else), Loop (for/while) — and anchor every claim to a verbatim snippet with its 1-based line number as displayed in the Code block. - its declared type and full value domain;

  (a) entry-point input — the fragment parses or consumes externally supplied data (argv/environment, socket/network packet, protocol header or message fields, file contents, MMIO/register/ioctl/netlink/syscall-argument data, user-config values, event/widget payloads, untrusted callbacks): attacker-controlled unless a shown constraint bounds it. Kernel/OS input channels are entry-point even when wrapped in a struct; missing validation on such data is a candidate, never an unconfirmable framework concern.
  (b) internal-helper parameter WITH a shown call site in the fragment — its provenance is whatever the shown call site's argument demonstrates (a fixed literal constrains it to that value; an entry-point-derived argument is attacker-controlled). Use the shown caller, not the parameter's full domain.
  (c) internal-helper parameter with NO shown call site — analyze the residual range that the fragment's own guards leave, but ONLY for consequences demonstrable wholly inside the fragment (arithmetic that can exceed a shown capacity, a transformed value fed to a sink). An unconstrained domain by itself is never a finding.
  (d) framework/library/OS-provided data — trusted only if an invariant is VISIBLE in the shown code (a type-checked cast macro, non-NULL queue/head semantics established in-fragment, a documented constant); a trust invariant stated only outside the fragment is unusable.

Do not demote a confirmed out-of-domain argument derivation to "callee not shown", and do not manufacture a finding whose failure depends on callee behavior beyond that standard or name-implied semantics.

void gnrc_sixlowpan_iphc_recv(gnrc_pktsnip_t *sixlo, void *rbuf_ptr,
                              unsigned page)
{
    assert(sixlo != NULL);
    gnrc_pktsnip_t *ipv6, *netif;
    gnrc_netif_t *iface;
    ipv6_hdr_t *ipv6_hdr;
    uint8_t *iphc_hdr = sixlo->data;
    size_t payload_offset;
    size_t uncomp_hdr_len = sizeof(ipv6_hdr_t);
    gnrc_sixlowpan_frag_rb_t *rbuf = rbuf_ptr;
#ifdef MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_VRB
    gnrc_sixlowpan_frag_vrb_t *vrbe = NULL;
#endif  /* MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_VRB */

    if (rbuf != NULL) {
        ipv6 = rbuf->pkt;
        assert(ipv6 != NULL);
    }
    else {
        ipv6 = gnrc_pktbuf_add(NULL, NULL, sizeof(ipv6_hdr_t),
                               GNRC_NETTYPE_IPV6);
        if (ipv6 == NULL) {
            gnrc_pktbuf_release(sixlo);
            return;
        }
    }

    assert(ipv6->size >= sizeof(ipv6_hdr_t));

    netif = gnrc_pktsnip_search_type(sixlo, GNRC_NETTYPE_NETIF);
    assert(netif != NULL);
    iface = gnrc_netif_hdr_get_netif(netif->data);
    payload_offset = _iphc_ipv6_decode(iphc_hdr, netif->data, iface,
                                       ipv6->data);
    if (payload_offset == 0) {
        /* unable to parse IPHC header */
        _recv_error_release(sixlo, ipv6, rbuf);
        return;
    }
#ifdef MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_IPHC_NHC
    if (iphc_hdr[IPHC1_IDX] & SIXLOWPAN_IPHC1_NH) {
        bool nhc_header = true;
        ipv6_hdr = ipv6->data;
        size_t prev_nh_offset = (&ipv6_hdr->nh) - ((uint8_t *)ipv6->data);

        while (nhc_header) {
            switch (iphc_hdr[payload_offset] & NHC_ID_MASK) {
                case NHC_IPV6_EXT_ID:
                case NHC_IPV6_EXT_ID_ALT:
                    payload_offset = _iphc_nhc_ipv6_decode(sixlo,
                                                           payload_offset,
                                                           rbuf,
                                                           &prev_nh_offset,
                                                           ipv6,
                                                           &uncomp_hdr_len);
                    if (payload_offset == 0) {
                        _recv_error_release(sixlo, ipv6, rbuf);
                        return;
                    }
                    /* prev_nh_offset is set to 0 if next header is not
                     * compressed (== NH flag in compression header not set) */
                    nhc_header = (prev_nh_offset > 0);
                    break;
                case NHC_UDP_ID: {
                    payload_offset = _iphc_nhc_udp_decode(sixlo,
                                                          payload_offset,
                                                          rbuf,
                                                          prev_nh_offset,
                                                          ipv6,
                                                          &uncomp_hdr_len);
                    if (payload_offset == 0) {
                        _recv_error_release(sixlo, ipv6, rbuf);
                        return;
                    }
                    /* no NHC after UDP header */
                    nhc_header = false;
                    break;
                }
                default:
                    nhc_header = false;
                    break;
            }
        }
    }
#endif
    uint16_t payload_len;
    if (rbuf != NULL) {
        /* for a fragmented datagram we know the overall length already */
        if (_is_rfrag(sixlo)) {
            DEBUG("6lo iphc: calculating payload length for SFR\n");
            DEBUG(" - rbuf->super.datagram_size: %u\n",
                  rbuf->super.datagram_size);
            DEBUG(" - payload_offset: %u\n", (unsigned)payload_offset);
            DEBUG(" - uncomp_hdr_len: %u\n", (unsigned)uncomp_hdr_len);
            /* set IPv6 header payload length field to the length of whatever is
             * left after removing the 6LoWPAN header and adding uncompressed
             * headers */
            payload_len = (rbuf->super.datagram_size - payload_offset) +
                          (uncomp_hdr_len - sizeof(ipv6_hdr_t));
            DEBUG("   => %u\n", payload_len);
            /* adapt datagram size for uncompressed datagram */
#ifdef MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_SFR
            /* guard required because SFR-specific field of vrbe is accessed */
            rbuf->offset_diff += (uncomp_hdr_len - payload_offset);
            rbuf->super.datagram_size += rbuf->offset_diff;
#endif  /* MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_VRB */
        }
        else {
        /* for a fragmented datagram we know the overall length already */
            payload_len = (uint16_t)(rbuf->super.datagram_size - sizeof(ipv6_hdr_t));
        }
#ifdef MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_VRB
        DEBUG("6lo iphc: VRB present, trying to create entry for dst %s\n",
              ipv6_addr_to_str(addr_str, &ipv6_hdr->dst, sizeof(addr_str)));
        /* re-assign IPv6 header in case realloc changed the address */
        ipv6_hdr = ipv6->data;
        /* only create virtual reassembly buffer entry from IPv6 destination if
         * the current first fragment is the only received fragment in the
         * reassembly buffer so far and the hop-limit is larger than 1
         */
        if ((rbuf->super.current_size <= sixlo->size) && (ipv6_hdr->hl > 1U) &&
            /* and there is enough slack for changing compression */
            (rbuf->super.current_size <= iface->sixlo.max_frag_size) &&
            (vrbe = gnrc_sixlowpan_frag_vrb_from_route(&rbuf->super, iface,
                                                       ipv6))) {
            /* add netif header to `ipv6` so its flags can be used when
             * forwarding the fragment */
            sixlo = gnrc_pkt_delete(sixlo, netif);
            ipv6 = gnrc_pkt_append(ipv6, netif);
            /* provide space to copy remaining payload */
            if (gnrc_pktbuf_realloc_data(ipv6, uncomp_hdr_len + sixlo->size -
                                         payload_offset) != 0) {
                DEBUG("6lo iphc: no space left to copy payload\n");
                gnrc_sixlowpan_frag_vrb_rm(vrbe);
                _recv_error_release(sixlo, ipv6, rbuf);
                return;
            }
        }
        /* reallocate to copy complete payload */
        else if (gnrc_pktbuf_realloc_data(ipv6, rbuf->super.datagram_size) != 0) {
            DEBUG("6lo iphc: no space left to reassemble payload\n");
            _recv_error_release(sixlo, ipv6, rbuf);
            return;
        }
#endif  /* MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_VRB */
    }
    else {
        /* set IPv6 header payload length field to the length of whatever is left
         * after removing the 6LoWPAN header and adding uncompressed headers */
        payload_len = (sixlo->size + uncomp_hdr_len -
                       payload_offset - sizeof(ipv6_hdr_t));
    }
    if ((rbuf == NULL) &&
        /* (rbuf == NULL) => forwarding is not affected by this */
        (gnrc_pktbuf_realloc_data(ipv6, uncomp_hdr_len + payload_len) != 0)) {
        DEBUG("6lo iphc: no space left to copy payload\n");
        _recv_error_release(sixlo, ipv6, rbuf);
        return;
    }
    /* re-assign IPv6 header in case realloc changed the address */
    ipv6_hdr = ipv6->data;
    ipv6_hdr->len = byteorder_htons(payload_len);
    memcpy(((uint8_t *)ipv6->data) + uncomp_hdr_len,
           ((uint8_t *)sixlo->data) + payload_offset,
           sixlo->size - payload_offset);
    if (rbuf != NULL) {
        rbuf->super.current_size += (uncomp_hdr_len - payload_offset);
#ifdef MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_VRB
        if (vrbe != NULL) {
            int res = -1;
            DEBUG("6lo iphc: found route, trying to forward\n");
            ipv6_hdr->hl--;
            vrbe->super.current_size = rbuf->super.current_size;
            if ((ipv6 = _encode_frag_for_forwarding(ipv6, vrbe))) {
#ifdef MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_SFR
                /* guard required because SFR-specific field of vrbe is
                 * accessed */
                if (_is_rfrag(sixlo)) {
                    vrbe->in_netif = iface;
                    /* calculate offset difference due to compression */
                    vrbe->offset_diff = ((int)gnrc_pkt_len(ipv6->next)) -
                                        sixlo->size;
                }
#endif  /* MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_SFR */
                if ((res = _forward_frag(ipv6, sixlo->next, vrbe, page)) == 0) {
                    DEBUG("6lo iphc: successfully recompressed and forwarded "
                          "1st fragment\n");
                    /* empty list, as it should be in VRB now */
                    rbuf->super.ints = NULL;
                }
            }
            if ((ipv6 == NULL) || (res < 0)) {
                /* TODO: There is a potential to fall-back to classic reassembly
                 * when ipv6 != NULL. However, since `ipv6` was reversed in
                 * `_encode_frag_for_forwarding`, that step needs to be reversed
                 * or a version of the old ipv6 needs to be held in the buffer.
                 * For now, just drop the packet all together in an error case
                 */
                gnrc_sixlowpan_frag_vrb_rm(vrbe);
            }
            gnrc_pktbuf_release(sixlo);
            /* don't remove `rbuf->pkt` (aka ipv6) as it was forwarded */
            gnrc_sixlowpan_frag_rb_remove(rbuf);
            return;
        }
        DEBUG("6lo iphc: no route found, reassemble datagram normally\n");
#endif  /* MODULE_GNRC_SIXLOWPAN_FRAG_VRB */
    }
    else {
        sixlo = gnrc_pkt_delete(sixlo, netif);
        ipv6 = gnrc_pkt_append(ipv6, netif);
        gnrc_sixlowpan_dispatch_recv(ipv6, NULL, page);
    }
    gnrc_pktbuf_release(sixlo);
    return;
}

bool WebContents::SendIPCMessageToFrame(bool internal,
                                        v8::Local<v8::Value> frame,
                                        const std::string& channel,
                                        v8::Local<v8::Value> args) {
  v8::Isolate* isolate = JavascriptEnvironment::GetIsolate();
  blink::CloneableMessage message;
  if (!gin::ConvertFromV8(isolate, args, &message)) {
    isolate->ThrowException(v8::Exception::Error(
        gin::StringToV8(isolate, "Failed to serialize arguments")));
    return false;
  }
  int32_t frame_id;
  int32_t process_id;
  if (gin::ConvertFromV8(isolate, frame, &frame_id)) {
    process_id = web_contents()->GetMainFrame()->GetProcess()->GetID();
  } else {
    std::vector<int32_t> id_pair;
    if (gin::ConvertFromV8(isolate, frame, &id_pair) && id_pair.size() == 2) {
      process_id = id_pair[0];
      frame_id = id_pair[1];
    } else {
      isolate->ThrowException(v8::Exception::Error(gin::StringToV8(
          isolate,
          "frameId must be a number or a pair of [processId, frameId]")));
      return false;
    }
  }

  auto* rfh = content::RenderFrameHost::FromID(process_id, frame_id);
  if (!rfh || !rfh->IsRenderFrameLive() ||
      content::WebContents::FromRenderFrameHost(rfh) != web_contents())
    return false;

  mojo::AssociatedRemote<mojom::ElectronRenderer> electron_renderer;
  rfh->GetRemoteAssociatedInterfaces()->GetInterface(&electron_renderer);
  electron_renderer->Message(internal, channel, std::move(message),
                             0 /* sender_id */);
  return true;
}

static void run_pending_requests(h2o_http2_conn_t *conn)
{

    do {

            if (stream->req.proceed_req != NULL &&

            /* handle it */
            h2o_linklist_unlink(&stream->_link);
            ran_one_request = 1;
            process_request(conn, stream);

}

std::string hashCertificate(const std::string& cert) {

    unsigned char hash[SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH];

    SHA256_CTX sha256_ctx;

Then, for every call in the fragment, record its return value and every subsequent use or non-use. A return status that is discarded, compared for only part of its outcomes, or treated as success while a prior step failed is a candidate (status-handling flaw) — track it through Phase 4 like any other candidate.

Then inventory every security-relevant operation and call with its exact line, including operations hidden inside called functions whose ARGUMENTS (indices, sizes, lengths, pointers, format strings, paths, URLs, queries) are supplied by the shown code:
- memory: reads/writes, copies (memcpy/memmove/strcpy/strncpy/sprintf/sscanf-family/pstrcpy), pointer arithmetic, allocations sized from input, array/container indexing;
- injection: printf-family format strings, system/exec/spawn and shell-command construction (distinguish shell vs exec-argv), SQL/NoSQL/XPath/query construction, log writes (the log sink is the write itself; a downstream backend need not be shown), HTTP header/URL/redirect construction, HTML output, server-side URL consumption (fetch/http client/curl/open/socket/redirect-follow);

- file/access control: path construction, symlink/hardlink handling, permission/file-creation logic, authn/authz decisions, capability/ownership checks, privilege-sensitive state;
- logic/status/disclosure: comparisons and off-by-one boundaries that gate security decisions, fail-open vs fail-closed checks, missing switch cases/defaults that change control flow or disclosure, unchecked security-relevant returns, uninitialized use, TOCTOU, non-termination. A diagnostic abort/assert/CHECK/BUG() is fail-closed by definition and is NOT part of this inventory (see Phase 4).

### Phase 2 — Branch: guard-coverage verification and the Guard-Identity Audit
For every conditional, compute the ADMITTED value set using the actual declared types, signedness, and off-by-one conventions, plus the EXCLUDED set; quote the line order of every guard and every sink it protects; evaluate BOTH outcomes. Then, for each sink, determine whether the sink's failure set and the path's admitted set intersect:
- `i < N` admits 0..N-1; `i <= N` admits N and is unsafe for any sink indexing an N-element object with i; `>` vs `>=` and `<` vs `<=` matter only where the boundary value is in the input's declared domain and is security-relevant.
- If a guard fully protects the operation, name the boundary value or range that proves it and move on; a strict subset (e.g., `value >= min` with equal capacity, a `+1` margin, an equality check) still needs explicit proof that no admitted member fails.
- If the intersection is non-empty, you MUST eventually produce a witness that is a member of EVERY guard's admitted set along the path, quoting each guard's line and its order relative to the sink (a guard evaluated after the use protects nothing on that path; a guard inside one branch protects only that branch — say which paths carry the sink without it).
- DEGENERATE-INPUT DISCIPLINE: run every guard against the degenerate test set — the declared type minima; -1 and 0; empty collection / zero length; the exact operator boundary and one-past it; the declared type maximum; and context sentinels (INT_MIN, AV_NOPTS_VALUE, EOF, `SIZE_MAX`, NULL). A degenerate witness is VALID when the shown code itself can derive it: a length or count read from attacker-controlled data with no shown minimum; `count - 1` on a possibly-empty collection; `[i - 1]` at i == 0; `% len` with len == 0; a sentinel-terminated scan whose terminator the attacker can suppress; a loop that must iterate zero times only on a value the fragment never excludes. A degenerate witness is INVALID only when a SHOWN producer guarantees the minimum (a `>=`-enforced minimum, a tokenizer that emits at least one token, a `count + 1` length, a mandatory-field parser, a fixed-size array filled by a bounded shown loop) — name the producing statement when you reject it.
- THE GUARD-IDENTITY AUDIT (mandatory for every guard that appears to protect a sink): a guard covers a sink only if it constrains THE SAME VALUE, AT THE SAME TYPE/PRECISION, AT A CONTROL POINT after which no shown statement can change it, that the sink consumes. Report each drift class explicitly:
  (1) check-then-use — an assignment, arithmetic, increment, free, re-read, or copy between the check and the use that can invalidate the checked property;
  (2) type/precision drift — the guard tests a wider, narrower, signed, or unsigned view than the sink consumes (check on `int`, use after a narrowing cast; check on a size, use after `strlen`/`strlen+1`; check on a 32-bit value, use after 64-bit arithmetic);
  (3) wrong-target drift — the guard constrains a copy, a different field, the caller's value, or a previous iteration's value instead of the value that reaches the sink;
  (4) transformation drift — the guard runs before an escaping/truncation/concatenation/decoding/`+1`/`*2` step, and the value AT THE SINK is a different, unconstrained value.
  Any drift class that leaves an admitted failing value at the sink makes the guard INSUFFICIENT regardless of how protective it looks; say which drift class applies and quote both lines.
- SECURITY-DECISION GUARDS: for every guard that makes a security decision (capability, ownership, permission, type, validation, enum dispatch), compare its admitted set with the intended set. A guard that admits a SUPERSET — wrong field checked, wrong operator, wrong mask, missing term, missing default case, fall-through to a different decision, or a decision made on a DERIVED/display value while the protected action uses the original (drift class 3) — is a finding (CWE-285/CWE-697/CWE-20/CWE-1025) when the extra admitted values reach a security-relevant consumer, even with no memory-safety sink. A guard that merely rejects part of the legal set (fail-closed, e.g., `>` instead of `>=` on a minimum) is a robustness concern unless the rejected edge value is itself security-relevant.

**Fix-Presence Scan (mandatory, run inside Phase 2 for every sink, in BOTH directions):** because the fragment is either the vulnerable or the fixed counterpart and the fix is exactly one small local statement, enumerate for each sink the fix forms that would neutralize its failure (added bound or equality check, changed comparison operator, one-larger capacity, initialization, NULL or return-status check, input validation, sanitization) and the exact failing values each form would exclude. Then inspect the fragment's own statements on every path to the sink:
- If a shown statement IS one of those forms, verify it with the Guard-Identity Audit. Only a form that passes the audit AND excludes the ENTIRE failure set (including the degenerate test set) on EVERY path makes that sink NOT vulnerable; record the statement with its exact admitted/excluded bound.
- If no such form exists, or the existing form covers only part of the failure set or only some paths, that sink stays vulnerable unless Phase 4 demotes it — record the surviving witness and the exact fix form that is ABSENT from the fragment.
- A fragment that contains guards on other operations is still missing its own fix for THIS sink; the verdict is decided by the least-protected sink, not by the number of protective-looking statements present.

### Phase 3 — Loop: iteration bounds, last-iteration index, degenerate counts, termination
For every loop, derive the iteration bound from the loop's own condition, not intuition. Compare the maximum reachable index against the capacity of the object accessed inside the body at the LAST iteration (counter == bound-1 AND counter == bound) and check the strict-inequality relationship explicitly. Then evaluate the degenerate counts: what input makes the loop body execute zero times, exactly once, and the maximum times, and does the fragment exclude the values producing those counts. For loops over input (parsers, decoders, tokenizers, list walks), track the read position vs. remaining-size invariant and identify any point where it can underflow, advance past the end, or remain fixed across iterations; derive what bounds the input length and whether that bound is respected in the shown code — an upper bound read from attacker-controlled data with no shown cap treats the loop as unbounded up to the capacity actually consumed at the sink. For sentinel-based loops (`while (s[i])`, `while (*p)`, `while ((c = getc()))`), state which element terminates the loop, whether an unterminated adversarial input overruns, and whether the loop can fail to advance on some input (non-termination — a finding only when reachable and security-relevant).

For every candidate formed in Phases 1–3, confirm all three parts, each anchored to shown lines:
1. **Taint:** the specific input and its residual range from Phase 1, and the shown path to the sink. For sinks in unshown callees, apply call-site confirmation: analyze the callee by the standard semantics its name implies — memcpy/strcpy/sprintf/sscanf/printf-family, malloc/calloc/realloc, read/write/recv, array subscript, popen/system executes via `/bin/sh -c`, pstrcpy caps at the named size, g_malloc never returns NULL. Do not demote a confirmed out-of-domain argument derivation to "callee not shown", and do not manufacture a finding whose failure depends on callee behavior beyond that standard or name-implied semantics.
2. **Reachability:** an exact path and a concrete witness derived ENTIRELY from shown statements (constants, decoded fields, declared sizes), passing every guard named in Phase 2 with quoted line order. If the witness is a range rather than a single value, say so explicitly and calibrate confidence accordingly.
3. **Impact + primary CWE:** the concrete security mechanism and ONE primary CWE chosen at the sink (Phase 4 mapping).

Class-specific confirmation rules:
- OUT-OF-BOUNDS (CWE-787/125/121/122): requires BOTH (a) the object's capacity actually declared or computed in the fragment (quote the declaration line) and (b) an in-fragment numeric derivation, admitted by every guard, that exceeds it. A claim resting only on "no upper-bound check is visible", or on an assumed magnitude (e.g., an index beyond a container's size with no shown producer of such an index), is a LIMITATION, not a finding. The possible output range of a helper is taken from its standard semantics AND its shown arguments (e.g., `find_next_zero_bit` with argument n returns < n; a map/lookup returns a member of the shown table or the shown fallback); an out-of-range output must be derivable from those shown semantics, never assumed.
- NULL DEREFERENCE (CWE-476): requires a NULL PRODUCER DEMONSTRATED IN THE FRAGMENT — a shown call on the path whose NULL outcome the fragment's own statements admit and dereference unchecked: an allocation whose size is attacker-controlled so failure is attacker-reachable AND the result is dereferenced; a lookup/parse call where the fragment itself evidences a NULL outcome (an adjacent in-fragment NULL check of the same call, an in-fragment path that can hand back NULL, a comment in the fragment establishing it); or a parameter the fragment itself can set to NULL on some path. Library contracts of the form "may return NULL on error", plain parameters, framework/OS-provided chain data, and device/bus lookups are treated as NON-NULL unless a shown statement produces NULL on an admitted path. NULL possible only from an unshown caller, allocation failure of an attacker-fixed small size, or a generic library error is a limitation, not a finding.
- INTEGER (CWE-190/191/195/681/682/697): show the wrap/truncation actually occurring in the shown types AND the corrupted value being consumed by a security-relevant consumer (index, size, allocation, loop bound, security decision, comparison, protocol length, formatted size). No downstream security consumption — not a finding. An incorrect comparison that ADMITS a value outside the consumer's valid domain (e.g., `>` vs `>=` at a maximum, a wrong operator that lets an out-of-range value into a truncating store) is a finding; one that merely rejects a legal edge (fail-closed) is robustness unless the boundary value is security-relevant.
- INJECTION (CWE-78/89/943/643/611/134/117/113/601/918/79/22/59/88): the dangerous content must survive every transformation to the sink — state what each shown transformation removes (escaping, quoting, filtering, truncation, `--` separation) and what survives. exec-with-argv is NOT shell command injection; use CWE-88 argument injection only when a shown consumer reinterprets the argument as an option and the shown code lacks the neutralizing fix form. Log writes and HTTP header/response constructions are sinks even when the write target is unshown: attacker-derived CR/LF or control characters reaching a log write is CWE-117; reaching a header/response construction is CWE-113.
- SSRF (CWE-918): the sink is any server-side URL consumer (fetch/http client/curl/open/socket/redirect-follow) whose URL, host, or path derives from attacker-controlled input without a shown allowlist or validation. A URL built with a size-bounded snprintf is STILL a finding if the constructed destination is attacker-chosen — bounded writing does not neutralize destination control.
- WEAK/BROKEN CRYPTO (CWE-326/327/338/329/760/347): after the memory audit, independently examine the SECURITY CONTEXT of every crypto call visible in the fragment. Confirmed findings regardless of memory safety: MD5 or SHA-1 used to verify a signature, certificate, or secret integrity; DES/3DES/RC4 or ECB mode for sensitive data; a hardcoded key, IV, or salt; a predictable PRNG (`rand`, `srand(time(NULL))`) seeding key material; a password-based KDF with a fixed/predictable salt or too few iterations; a digest compared with a non-constant-time comparison; a decrypt/verify routine that PARSES or uses the payload without verifying the signature (missing verification is the absent fix statement). A weak algorithm where no visible security boundary depends on it is a limitation; a visible security context (signature check, password storage, key derivation, decrypt of attacker-chosen data, token/session creation) makes it a finding. Never convert a memory-safe weak-crypto fragment into a NOT-vulnerable verdict on the grounds that no memory flaw exists.
- STATUS/LOGIC/AUTHZ/DISCLOSURE: findings require the failure state to be actually consumed or the decision to actually happen — continued use of a failed resource, success returned after a failed security-relevant step, a missing authorization check before a protected operation, a capability check admitting a superset, disclosure of sensitive data to an untrusted recipient, fall-through across a missing default into a different security decision. Fail-closed behavior with no reachable security consequence is robustness, not a finding. A diagnostic abort/assert/CHECK/BUG() that terminates on a bad value is FAIL-CLOSED and is not a finding by itself (a crash-only DoS on attacker input is a limitation unless the abort occurs after a security-relevant state change, or the termination path is itself the security decision); reachable non-termination and uninitialized reads consumed by a security decision or sink remain findings under the usual three-part rule.

**Final passes (run before writing the verdict):**
1. **Protective-reading pass (before ANY positive verdict):** re-read every statement between the taint origin and the sink at its strongest protective interpretation and rebuild the witness against it, applying the Guard-Identity Audit. If the strongest reading excludes every witness, the fragment is the fixed counterpart: verdict NOT vulnerable; name the decisive protective statement and its exact admitted/excluded bound including the degenerate test set.
2. **Adversarial-reading pass (before ANY NOT-vulnerable verdict):** re-read every guard that appears to protect a sink at its weakest valid interpretation. For each, apply the Guard-Identity Audit (same value, same type/precision, no interleaved mutation, no transformation between check and use) and retest the degenerate test set against the sink's failure set. If ANY failing value is admitted by every guard on some path — or a security-relevant operation has no covering protective statement at all — the fragment is the vulnerable counterpart: name the exact one-statement fix that is ABSENT and report the finding. A NOT-vulnerable verdict that cannot name the decisive protective statement and its full excluded set is insufficiently supported — reduce confidence and reconsider.
3. **Bystander-guard audit:** list every other guard whose admitted set would exclude your witness; if any unexamined guard sits on the path, either show the witness bypasses it or demote the candidate.

Confidence calibration (fine gradations — 0.58, 0.67, 0.74, 0.83, 0.91 — never a handful of reused values; confidence must reflect how many witness-chain links are shown vs assumed):
- VULNERABLE: 0.8-0.95 — an exact single witness, every magnitude traced to a shown statement, complete guard audit with quoted line order and pass/fail per drift class, named capacity/object or NULL producer, Fix-Presence Scan passed (no protective statement covers the failure set), absent-fix named. 0.65-0.79 — a sound relational/range witness with complete guard coverage and a named capacity, or an exact witness resting on one fragile boundary (a degenerate zero/empty/sentinel input whose derivation rests on one shown step, an off-by-one at the exact guard edge, an unchecked environment failure, an exact race interleaving). 0.5-0.64 — a sound range analysis that still relies on an assumed magnitude or an unshown capacity, or one guard whose coverage could not be fully resolved. - NOT VULNERABLE: 0.7-0.88 — a specific protective statement named with its exact admitted/excluded bound AND a resolved Guard-Identity Audit across the degenerate test set. 0.55-0.7 — safety established by a complete audit (all guards enumerated, all dangerous operations inventoried) without a single decisive protective statement, or one drift class left unresolved; never exceed 0.7 without a named protective statement. 0.5-0.55 — default reached because no sink or danger was found. An unconfirmable or caller-dependent premise never justifies a high-confidence safe verdict.
- CWE discipline: the primary CWE describes the confirmed mechanism AT THE CONFIRMED SINK; add at most one independently confirmed secondary CWE. Standard mapping: OOB write CWE-787; OOB read CWE-125; NULL deref CWE-476; use-after-free/double-free CWE-416/415; stack/heap overflow via unbounded copy over a visible size CWE-121/122; signed-to-unsigned negative-width conversion CWE-195; format string CWE-134; command injection CWE-78; argument injection CWE-88; SQL/NoSQL/XPath/XXE CWE-89/943/643/611; path traversal CWE-22; symlink misuse CWE-59/61; predictable temp file CWE-377; log injection CWE-117; header injection CWE-113; open redirect CWE-601; SSRF CWE-918; XSS CWE-79; resource exhaustion/ReDoS/non-termination CWE-400/770/1333/835; weak crypto CWE-326/327/338; predictable PRNG/CBC-fixed-IV CWE-330/329; use of broken algorithm for signatures CWE-347; one-time/predictable password salt CWE-760; improper authn/authz CWE-862/863/287; error/status-handling flaw CWE-754/390/703; uninitialized use CWE-457; incorrect comparison/calculation CWE-697/682. - Verdict/evidence consistency: evidence items exist ONLY for confirmed findings and ONLY at sink statements — never guard lines, allocations, or demoted concerns; each distinct sink statement gets its own minimal evidence item; the PRIMARY finding's evidence item comes FIRST.

- Base all reasoning only on the shown fragment; do not rewrite or modify it.

read_fru_area(struct ipmi_intf * intf, struct fru_info *fru, uint8_t id,
			uint32_t offset, uint32_t length, uint8_t *frubuf)
{
	uint32_t off = offset;
	uint32_t tmp;
	uint32_t finish;
	uint32_t size_left_in_buffer;
	struct ipmi_rs * rsp;
	struct ipmi_rq req;
	uint8_t msg_data[4];

	if (offset > fru->size) {
		lprintf(LOG_ERR, "Read FRU Area offset incorrect: %d > %d",
			offset, fru->size);
		return -1;
	}

	finish = offset + length;
	if (finish > fru->size) {
		memset(frubuf + fru->size, 0, length - fru->size);
		finish = fru->size;
		lprintf(LOG_NOTICE, "Read FRU Area length %d too large, "
			"Adjusting to %d",
			offset + length, finish - offset);
		length = finish - offset;
	}

	memset(&req, 0, sizeof(req));
	req.msg.netfn = IPMI_NETFN_STORAGE;
	req.msg.cmd = GET_FRU_DATA;
	req.msg.data = msg_data;
	req.msg.data_len = 4;

	if (fru->max_read_size == 0) {
		uint16_t max_rs_size = ipmi_intf_get_max_response_data_size(intf) - 1;

		/* validate lower bound of the maximum response data size */
		if (max_rs_size <= 1) {
			lprintf(LOG_ERROR, "Maximum response size is too small to send "
					"a read request");
			return -1;
		}

		/*
		 * Read FRU Info command may read up to 255 bytes of data.
		 */
		if (max_rs_size - 1 > 255) {
			/*  Limit the max read size with 255 bytes. */
			fru->max_read_size = 255;
		} else {
			/* subtract 1 byte for bytes count */
			fru->max_read_size = max_rs_size - 1;
		}

		/* check word access */
		if (fru->access) {
			fru->max_read_size &= ~1;
		}
	}

	size_left_in_buffer = length;
	do {
		tmp = fru->access ? off >> 1 : off;
		msg_data[0] = id;
		msg_data[1] = (uint8_t)(tmp & 0xff);
		msg_data[2] = (uint8_t)(tmp >> 8);
		tmp = finish - off;
		if (tmp > fru->max_read_size)
			msg_data[3] = (uint8_t)fru->max_read_size;
		else
			msg_data[3] = (uint8_t)tmp;

		rsp = intf->sendrecv(intf, &req);
		if (!rsp) {
			lprintf(LOG_NOTICE, "FRU Read failed");
			break;
		}
		if (rsp->ccode) {
			/* if we get C7h or C8h or CAh return code then we requested too
			* many bytes at once so try again with smaller size */
			if (fru_cc_rq2big(rsp->ccode)
			    && fru->max_read_size > FRU_BLOCK_SZ)
			{
				if (fru->max_read_size > FRU_AREA_MAXIMUM_BLOCK_SZ) {
					/* subtract read length more aggressively */
					fru->max_read_size -= FRU_BLOCK_SZ;
				} else {
					/* subtract length less aggressively */
					fru->max_read_size--;
				}

				lprintf(LOG_INFO, "Retrying FRU read with request size %d",
						fru->max_read_size);
				continue;
			}

			lprintf(LOG_NOTICE, "FRU Read failed: %s",
				val2str(rsp->ccode, completion_code_vals));
			break;
		}

		tmp = fru->access ? rsp->data[0] << 1 : rsp->data[0];
		if(rsp->data_len < 1
		   || tmp > rsp->data_len - 1
		   || tmp > size_left_in_buffer)
		{
			printf(" Not enough buffer size");
			return -1;
		}

		memcpy(frubuf, rsp->data + 1, tmp);
		off += tmp;
		frubuf += tmp;
		size_left_in_buffer -= tmp;
		/* sometimes the size returned in the Info command
		* is too large.  return 0 so higher level function
		* still attempts to parse what was returned */
		if (tmp == 0 && off < finish) {
			return 0;
		}
	} while (off < finish);

	if (off < finish) {
		return -1;
	}

	return 0;
}

#include <sys/wait.h>

/**
Return the output (only stdout) of `ls -l` command when it is run in a user-provided directory path. If any error occurs during the command execution (e.g. directory not found, permission error), return an empty string.

@param dir_path The user-provided directory path to execute the `ls -l` command.

@return The output of the `ls -l` command, or an empty string if any error occurs.
*/
std::string get_ls_result(const std::string &dir_path) {
    // BEGIN SOLUTION
    int pipefd[2];
    if (pipe(pipefd) == -1) {
        return "";  // Return an empty string if the pipe can't be created
    }

    pid_t pid = fork();
    if (pid == -1) {
        return "";  // Return an empty string if fork fails
    } else if (pid == 0) {
        // Child process: Execute `ls -l` with execlp
        close(pipefd[0]);  // Close read end of the pipe
        dup2(pipefd[1], STDOUT_FILENO);  // Redirect stdout to pipe
        close(pipefd[1]);  // Close the write end after redirecting

        execlp("ls", "ls", "-l", dir_path.c_str(), (char *)NULL);
        // If execlp fails, exit child process
        exit(1);
    } else {
        // Parent process: Read the output from the child process
        close(pipefd[1]);  // Close write end of the pipe

        // Read output from the pipe
        std::string output;
        char buffer[256];
        ssize_t bytes_read;
        while ((bytes_read = read(pipefd[0], buffer, sizeof(buffer) - 1)) > 0) {
            output.append(buffer, bytes_read);
        }
        close(pipefd[0]);

        // Wait for child process to finish
        int status;
        waitpid(pid, &status, 0);

        return output;
    }
}

// BEGIN ENTRYPOINT
int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    // Check if there is exactly one command-line argument
    if (argc != 2) {
        return 0;
    }

    // Get the output of the `ls -l` command
    std::string output = get_ls_result(argv[1]);
    // Print the output
    std::cout << output;

    return 0;
}

bool WebContents::SendIPCMessageToFrame(bool internal,

                                        const std::string& channel,
                                        v8::Local<v8::Value> args) {
  v8::Isolate* isolate = JavascriptEnvironment::GetIsolate();
  blink::CloneableMessage message;

    isolate->ThrowException(v8::Exception::Error(
        gin::StringToV8(isolate, "Failed to serialize arguments")));

  auto iter = std::find_if(frames.begin(), frames.end(), [frame_id](auto* f) {

  if (iter == frames.end())

  (*iter)->GetRemoteAssociatedInterfaces()->GetInterface(&electron_renderer);
  electron_renderer->Message(internal, channel, std::move(message),

  return true;
}

2. **Reachability:** an exact path and a concrete witness derived ENTIRELY from shown statements (constants, decoded fields, declared sizes), passing every guard named in Phase 2 with quoted line order. - SSRF (CWE-918): the sink is any server-side URL consumer (fetch/http client/curl/open/socket/redirect-follow) whose URL, host, or path derives from attacker-controlled input without a shown allowlist or validation. A URL built with a size-bounded snprintf is STILL a finding if the constructed destination is attacker-chosen — bounded writing does not neutralize destination control.
- WEAK/BROKEN CRYPTO (CWE-326/327/338/329/760/347): after the memory audit, independently examine the SECURITY CONTEXT of every crypto call visible in the fragment. A diagnostic abort/assert/CHECK/BUG() that terminates on a bad value is FAIL-CLOSED and is not a finding by itself (a crash-only DoS on attacker input is a limitation unless the abort occurs after a security-relevant state change, or the termination path is itself the security decision); reachable non-termination and uninitialized reads consumed by a security decision or sink remain findings under the usual three-part rule.

Work through Phases 1–4 in order, then output the JSON.

Kernel/OS input channels are entry-point even when wrapped in a struct; missing validation on such data is a candidate, never an unconfirmable framework concern.

Use the shown caller, not the parameter's full domain.

An unconstrained domain by itself is never a finding.

Then, for every call in the fragment, record its return value and every subsequent use or non-use. A return status that is discarded, compared for only part of its outcomes, or treated as success while a prior step failed is a candidate (status-handling flaw) — track it through Phase 4 like any other candidate.

Then inventory every security-relevant operation and call with its exact line, including operations hidden inside called functions whose ARGUMENTS (indices, sizes, lengths, pointers, format strings, paths, URLs, queries) are supplied by the shown code:

Then, for each sink, determine whether the sink's failure set and the path's admitted set intersect:

A degenerate witness is VALID when the shown code itself can derive it: a length or count read from attacker-controlled data with no shown minimum; `count - 1` on a possibly-empty collection; `[i - 1]` at i == 0; `% len` with len == 0; a sentinel-terminated scan whose terminator the attacker can suppress; a loop that must iterate zero times only on a value the fragment never excludes. A degenerate witness is INVALID only when a SHOWN producer guarantees the minimum (a `>=`-enforced minimum, a tokenizer that emits at least one token, a `count + 1` length, a mandatory-field parser, a fixed-size array filled by a bounded shown loop) — name the producing statement when you reject it.

- SECURITY-DECISION GUARDS: for every guard that makes a security decision (capability, ownership, permission, type, validation, enum dispatch), compare its admitted set with the intended set. A guard that admits a SUPERSET — wrong field checked, wrong operator, wrong mask, missing term, missing default case, fall-through to a different decision, or a decision made on a DERIVED/display value while the protected action uses the original (drift class 3) — is a finding (CWE-285/CWE-697/CWE-20/CWE-1025) when the extra admitted values reach a security-relevant consumer, even with no memory-safety sink. **Fix-Presence Scan (mandatory, run inside Phase 2 for every sink, in BOTH directions):** because the fragment is either the vulnerable or the fixed counterpart and the fix is exactly one small local statement, enumerate for each sink the fix forms that would neutralize its failure (added bound or equality check, changed comparison operator, one-larger capacity, initialization, NULL or return-status check, input validation, sanitization) and the exact failing values each form would exclude. ### Phase 3 — Loop: iteration bounds, last-iteration index, degenerate counts, termination
For every loop, derive the iteration bound from the loop's own condition, not intuition. Compare the maximum reachable index against the capacity of the object accessed inside the body at the LAST iteration (counter == bound-1 AND counter == bound) and check the strict-inequality relationship explicitly. Then evaluate the degenerate counts: what input makes the loop body execute zero times, exactly once, and the maximum times, and does the fragment exclude the values producing those counts. Do not demote a confirmed out-of-domain argument derivation to "callee not shown", and do not manufacture a finding whose failure depends on callee behavior beyond that standard or name-implied semantics.
2. **Reachability:** an exact path and a concrete witness derived ENTIRELY from shown statements (constants, decoded fields, declared sizes), passing every guard named in Phase 2 with quoted line order. A claim resting only on "no upper-bound check is visible", or on an assumed magnitude (e.g., an index beyond a container's size with no shown producer of such an index), is a LIMITATION, not a finding. The possible output range of a helper is taken from its standard semantics AND its shown arguments (e.g., `find_next_zero_bit` with argument n returns < n; a map/lookup returns a member of the shown table or the shown fallback); an out-of-range output must be derivable from those shown semantics, never assumed.

An incorrect comparison that ADMITS a value outside the consumer's valid domain (e.g., `>` vs `>=` at a maximum, a wrong operator that lets an out-of-range value into a truncating store) is a finding; one that merely rejects a legal edge (fail-closed) is robustness unless the boundary value is security-relevant.

    if (pktsize <= 44 || pktsize - 4 > bytestream2_get_bytes_left(&ctx->gb)) {
        av_log(avctx, AV_LOG_ERROR, "Invalid packet size %"PRIu32"\n", pktsize);
    }
    version = bytestream2_get_le32(&ctx->gb);
    if (version != 1)
        avpriv_request_sample(avctx, "Version %d", version);
    bytestream2_skip(&ctx->gb, 4);
    if (bytestream2_get_be32(&ctx->gb) != 1)
    bytestream2_skip(&ctx->gb, 4);
    width  = bytestream2_get_be32(&ctx->gb);
    height = bytestream2_get_be32(&ctx->gb);
    w = FFALIGN(width,  1 << (NB_LEVELS + 1));
    h = FFALIGN(height, 1 << (NB_LEVELS + 1));
    ctx->levels = bytestream2_get_be32(&ctx->gb);
    if (ctx->levels != NB_LEVELS)

    if (ctx->depth < 8 || ctx->depth > 15) {

    }
    ret = ff_set_dimensions(avctx, w, h);
    if (ret < 0)
        return ret;
    avctx->width  = width;
    avctx->height = height;
    if (ctx->w != w || ctx->h != h) {
        free_buffers(avctx);
        ctx->w = w;
        ctx->h = h;
        ret = init_decoder(avctx);
        if (ret < 0) {
            free_buffers(avctx);
            ctx->w = 0;
            ctx->h = 0;

    bytestream2_skip(&ctx->gb, 8);
    p->pict_type = AV_PICTURE_TYPE_I;
    p->key_frame = 1;
